topics.name: Data Curation
topics.subtitle: Reliable evidence begins with a defined dataset.
topics.body: Our work makes the decisions behind a biomedical dataset explicit: which chemical representations, assays, endpoints, units, and source records belong together. Dataset contracts, provenance, and quality diagnostics help turn heterogeneous pharmacology records into reproducible research assets.
topics.detail: Our accepted Digital Discovery paper presents a reusable, OECD-anchored curation and benchmarking framework demonstrated for opioid receptors. CURATO-OPIOID makes pharmacological mechanism and assay readout explicit before modeling, with traceable curated data, a versioned ontology, and scaffold-locked external validation.

topics.name: Contact Networks
topics.subtitle: Reading protein structure through its connections.
topics.body: A protein is more than a structural overlay or a binding pocket. We study how networks of residue contacts change across molecular states and related proteins, using topology-aware comparisons to locate gained and lost contacts throughout a protein domain.
topics.detail: Our CDK-family study examines how selective CDK5 inhibitors relate to contact redistribution near the ligand and in the distal C-lobe. These structural comparisons provide a quantitative view of selectivity and a foundation for testable medicinal-chemistry hypotheses.

figures.title: Contact-network phenotyping
figures.alt: CDK5 kinase-domain regions and a workflow comparing contact maps across 30 CDK structures.
figures.caption: Kinase-domain annotation connects residue-contact comparisons to region-level patterns across a panel of CDK structures.

figures.alt: CDK5 protein ribbon colored by kinase region, with a bar chart comparing contact-network changes within CDK5 and across related kinases.
figures.caption: A region map and contact-network comparisons place CDK5 in the context of related kinases, linking domain-level organization with the search for selectivity.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · JCIM (2026), Fig. 8 · CC BY 4.0

topics.name: Protein Timing
topics.subtitle: The kinetics clock: defining what a rate measures.
topics.body: Our kinetics-clock research asks how to obtain reproducible molecular transition measurements and when the available evidence supports a reported rate. State definitions, transition counting, sampling resolution, and uncertainty all contribute to the measurement.
topics.detail: In our alanine-dipeptide benchmark, two standard estimators agree closely when given matched states, while two conventional state definitions produce a larger difference on a fast transition. The work motivates publishing state definitions alongside reference rates and preregistering analysis rules before scoring measurements.

figures.title: A conformational landscape for the clock
figures.alt: Alanine-dipeptide Ramachandran free-energy map with core boundaries, based on 39.2 microseconds across 16 simulation replicas.
figures.caption: The alanine-dipeptide free-energy landscape used to benchmark conformational transitions. Dashed lines identify the core-state boundaries.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · ChemRxiv preprint (2026), Fig. 2 · Author figure

figures.title: State definition and estimator effects
figures.alt: Two-panel comparison of rates from the Hill relation and core-set milestoning under angular-core and distance-difference state definitions.
figures.caption: The same trajectories support a comparison of estimator choice and state definition on fast and slow transitions. Rates are interpreted together with the states they describe.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · ChemRxiv preprint (2026), Fig. 5 · Author figure

topics.name: Binding-Site Discovery
topics.subtitle: Finding binding opportunities in their biological context.
topics.body: We investigate where small molecules can bind and how protein structure, conformational changes, and the local environment shape those opportunities. Structural analysis and cosolvent mapping help us explore accessible, cryptic, and allosteric sites and develop hypotheses for molecular design.
topics.detail: FragFlow is one example of this work. Its depth-resolved reference accounts for probe partitioning within lipid bilayers when mapping membrane proteins. Studies of the ADP/ATP carrier, C5aR1, and TREK-1 connect local enrichment to an explicit environmental baseline and reproducible analysis rules.

figures.title: The membrane-depth reference
figures.alt: Depth-resolved benzene profiles, a cosolvent transfer-free-energy ladder, and bilayer occupancy compared with geometric baselines.
figures.caption: Probe partitioning and reference profiles vary with membrane depth. Individual replicas and probe-specific baselines keep those differences visible.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · FragFlow, Fig. 4 · Regenerated from released data and figure code · CC BY 4.0

figures.title: Testing the scoring reference
figures.alt: Detection-rate curves comparing depth-resolved and bulk-water references across AAC, C5aR1, and TREK-1 voxel populations.
figures.caption: Depth-resolved and scalar bulk-water references are compared on identical voxel populations. The curves show detection behavior across thresholds, including sites that do not pass the frozen rule.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · FragFlow, Fig. 5 · Regenerated from verified released data · CC BY 4.0

topics.name: Stereochemistry
topics.subtitle: Connecting three-dimensional molecular identity with recognition.
topics.body: We study stereochemistry as a central part of molecular identity and drug discovery. Our work combines conformational analysis, chiroptical spectroscopy, and electronic-structure calculations to support absolute-configuration assignments and assess the evidence behind them.
topics.detail: Our KChiro project compares experimental electronic circular dichroism with computed conformational ensembles. Spectral agreement, Cotton-effect sign patterns, and method sensitivity help us identify supported assignments and cases that require additional evidence. The protocol remains under development.

figures.title: Experimental and computed ECD
figures.alt: ECD spectra for three KChiro benchmark cases comparing sign-audited experiment with B3LYP, PBE0, and CAM-B3LYP calculations.
figures.caption: Representative experimental benchmarks and computed ensembles. Curves are amplitude-normalized for shape comparison; the experimental sign audit is applied and wavelengths are unshifted.
figures.credit: KChiro research project · Replotted from the original ensemble CSVs for readability

figures.title: Confirmation and abstention
figures.alt: KChiro protocol comparison on a seven-case frozen panel, with four confirmed cases and three abstentions under version 1.1.
figures.caption: The seven-case frozen panel reports four confirmations and three abstentions under protocol v1.1. These results describe this limited research panel; broader validation remains part of the developing method.
figures.credit: KChiro research project · Protocol v1.1 evaluation figure (2026)

topics.name: Conformational Search
topics.subtitle: Exploring molecular flexibility with explicit uncertainty.
topics.body: Flexible molecules can adopt multiple shapes, with consequences for molecular recognition and the interpretation of computed properties. We study how to build useful conformational ensembles, compare search strategies, and assess the sampling evidence behind an ensemble used in drug discovery.
topics.detail: Our CertCrest project combines independent replicated searches, conformer clustering, energy re-ranking, and statistical assessments of search coverage and ensemble populations. Declared energy windows, computational methods, solvent conditions, and stereochemical assumptions define the scope of each result. The workflow identifies when additional sampling is needed and records the evidence supporting its conclusions.

figures.title: Conformational search with explicit uncertainty
figures.alt: CertCrest concept workflow: define the search scope, repeat independent searches, cluster and re-rank conformers, assess coverage and population uncertainty, and report a bounded result or request further sampling.
figures.caption: CertCrest connects replicated conformational sampling to explicit assessments of coverage and population uncertainty. Conclusions are interpreted within the declared search conditions; additional sampling is an actionable outcome.
figures.credit: Our team · CertCrest research workflow schematic (2026)

topics.name: Molecular Design & Synthesis
topics.subtitle: Turning molecular insight into compounds we can test.
topics.body: Our team brings structure-guided design and synthetic chemistry together to develop bioactive molecules. In our CDK5 program for Alzheimer’s disease research, kinase contact-network comparisons inform hypotheses for selectivity, while modular synthesis lets us vary substituents and functional groups. We have prepared 46 small molecules across Boc-protected, free-base, imine, and amide series.
topics.detail: The synthetic route begins with N-alkylation or N-benzylation using alkyl or benzyl bromides and sodium hydride in DMF. Palladium-catalyzed C–N coupling with Brett-Phos Pd G3 and cesium carbonate builds the protected derivatives, followed by Boc removal and free-base preparation. We diversify amine intermediates through aldehyde condensation to form imines and HATU/DIPEA-mediated coupling with carboxylic acids to form amides.

figures.credit: Our team · Generic reaction schemes adapted from the CDK5 annual report
figures.title: CDK5 series assembly and deprotection
figures.alt: Generic reaction scheme showing N-substitution, palladium-catalyzed C–N coupling, and Boc deprotection followed by free-base preparation, with named reagents and no molecular structures.
figures.caption: N-substitution and palladium-catalyzed C–N coupling build the protected series. Deprotection and free-base preparation provide amine intermediates for further diversification.

figures.credit: Our team · Generic reaction schemes adapted from the CDK5 annual report
figures.title: Diversifying the CDK5 amine intermediates
figures.alt: Two generic reaction schemes: an amine and aromatic aldehyde form imine derivatives with molecular sieves, and an amine and carboxylic acid form amide derivatives using HATU and DIPEA. No molecular structures are shown.
figures.caption: Amine intermediates enter complementary synthetic routes: aldehyde condensation generates imines, while activated carboxylic-acid coupling generates amides. These transformations expand the chemical series for testing.

figures.title: CDK5 synthesis and testing workflow
figures.alt: Our CDK5 workflow: structure-guided design, synthesis of 46 compounds across four series, purification and NMR and HRMS characterization, ongoing CDK5/p25 testing, and future lead selection and optimization.
figures.caption: Our workflow connects structure-guided design and a 46-compound library with characterization and ongoing CDK5/p25 evaluation. Testing results will guide lead selection and the next optimization cycle.
figures.credit: Our team · CDK5 research workflow schematic (2026)

figures.title: A structural fingerprint for CDK5
figures.alt: Published comparisons of contact order, packing density, and hydrogen-bond network size across CDK5, CDK2, and CDK1 structures.
figures.caption: Contact order, packing density, and hydrogen-bond counts offer complementary views of the kinase structures used in the CDK5 project. These comparisons inform structural hypotheses for inhibitor discovery.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · JCIM (2026), Fig. 11 · CC BY 4.0

figures.title: Comparing the D144 contact shell
figures.alt: Changed-contact counts around CDK5 residue D144 across related kinase structures and partner states, showing means and standard deviations.
figures.caption: Cross-family contact-shell changes provide a structural comparison independent of the statistical-potential lookup. Values and sample sizes reproduce the published Figure 10 results.
figures.credit: Nael, Alakonda & Elokely · JCIM (2026), Fig. 10 · Replotted from published values · CC BY 4.0

additional: Purification, proton and carbon NMR, and high-resolution mass spectrometry establish the chemical identity of the compounds. Ongoing CDK5/p25 testing connects these synthetic series to biological evaluation and will guide lead selection and subsequent optimization. Potency and selectivity are still being established.

intro.hero: Our team connects computational modeling, chemical synthesis, and experimental evaluation to understand molecular recognition and develop bioactive compounds. We treat data quality, protein behavior, molecular flexibility, and stereochemistry as parts of the same discovery problem, so each calculation and experiment can inform the next design decision.
intro.title: An integrative approach to drug discovery.
paragraphs: Drug discovery depends on understanding how a compound’s chemistry, three-dimensional shape, and biological environment work together. Reliable measurements and molecular models help us interpret activity, investigate selectivity, and identify questions that experiments can resolve. Our approach connects these sources of evidence to build better-supported design hypotheses.

We begin by curating chemical and biological data, examining protein structure and behavior, and exploring molecular conformations and stereochemistry. These insights guide compound design and synthesis. We characterize the resulting molecules and evaluate their biological activity, then use the experimental findings to refine our models and the next set of designs.

This iterative connection between computation and experiment helps us prioritize informative studies, recognize uncertainty, and make the reasoning behind a discovery program reproducible. Our research develops methods and chemical strategies that can be adapted to different targets and therapeutic questions.
